text:
ash_support: FYI customer ACME reports large p95 regressions on /v1/embeddings since ~08:10 UTC, timeouts and 5xxs. p95 from ~700ms -> 2.3s. Opening thread to triage.

nate_oncall: I'm looking. grabbing perf graphs and recent infra changes. any deploys/driver rolls last night?

deploy-bot: deploy summary: kernel+driver patch v2.4.7 rolled to eu1 and eu2 at 03:45 UTC (canary->all).

mia_eng_sre: saw a cluster-wide bump in host io wait correlated with the roll. iostat on an affected node shows NVMe avg await jump: 
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz   await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         120.0   420.1  2048.0  8192.0   20.0     2.50   19.5   10.2   9.3   1.25  78.5
```

ash_support: customer also seeing occasional auth timeouts (401 -> 403 spike) during slow periods, might be cascading timeouts.

nate_oncall: can you paste a quick curl repro (one-liner) so we can reproduce from inside cluster?

sam_cs: here's a small repro we used: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -d '{\"input\":\"test\"}' -w \"time_total:%{time_total}\\nstatus:%{http_code}\\n'` . In eu1 hitting our hosted endpoint the time_total alternates 0.6s / 2.1s.

mia_eng_sre: i can reproduce from inside eu1: toggling large keys causes retries to pile up. suspect driver patch altered NVMe scheduler behavior or IO priority. dmesg has repeated warnings after patch: 
```
[ 1023.456789] nvme nvme0: I/O timeout, resetting controller
[ 1023.460001] nvme0n1: failed to abort command
```

nate_oncall: immediate mitigations proposed: 1) route ACME traffic to eu3 fallback pool, 2) reduce batch size/disable continuous batching for embeddings, 3) increase client-side auth timeout to avoid cascade, 4) drain and roll back driver on a small set of nodes to confirm. doing 1+2 now.

ash_support: please confirm before routing customer. i notified customer we're investigating and suggested temporary region failover.

mia_eng_sre: applied route override for ACME to eu3 (65% traffic) and set embeddings batch_size=1 for their tenant via feature flag. seeing p95 drop from 2.3s -> 680ms already.

ops-bot: action log: route_override applied for tenant ACME -> eu3, rollout id rr-2026-03-17-01. feature_flag batch_size=1 for tenant acme, id ff-9832.

nate_oncall: rolling back driver on 3 suspect eu1 nodes (drain -> reboot -> rollback). will report results in ~10m.

mia_eng_sre: quick note: increased KV cache TTL from 30s -> 120s for ACME to reduce repeated cold-start fetches.

ash_support: good. i updated the support ticket and told customer we routed ~65% of their traffic and will follow-up after rollback. customer ok with region failover for now.

nate_oncall: rollback completed on 3 nodes. early telemetry: host io await on those nodes returned to baseline, per-node p95 for embeddings decreased ~55%. still seeing some noisy nodes. next: schedule kernel/driver bisect (canary patch variants) and coordinate with infra vendor.

mia_eng_sre: logging ticket for vendor with dmesg snippets and iostat capture. ticket INFRA-1729. recommend hold on full patch rollout until we confirm bisect.

ash_support: follow-ups: 1) create postmortem if we don't have already, 2) customer post-update note + SLA credit eval, 3) devdocs for region-failover steps for Support.

nate_oncall: creating incident doc now and assigning owners. we'll add mitigation runbook steps we used (route override, batch_size flag, KV cache tweak, targeted rollback).

sam_cs: customer happy with quick mitigation. asks for ETA on full fix/rollback confirmation.

mia_eng_sre: ETA for bisect + vendor call: 48h. will update support thread.

ash_support: thanks all. marking as active/triage; adding postmortem tag. :thumbsup:
